correctness.rationale: On a directed n-cycle every variable-free formula is rotation invariant, so nested tests are uniformly true or false for each n. A simultaneous formula/program induction can partition n by finitely many previously established test truth profiles and reduce each test profile to a fixed test-free regular language over a,a^-1. Its signed displacement set is an effective finite union of integer linear sets b+ΣN v_j by effective Parikh semilinearity. In the finite additive group Z/nZ, the subsemigroup generated by the signed steps equals their subgroup, since each inverse step is a nonnegative multiple modulo n. Therefore some component yields a return iff gcd(n,v_1,...,v_s) divides b, including empty, zero and negative-generator cases (if all v_j=0, n|b). For nonzero d=gcd(|v_j|), gcd(n,d)|b is a Boolean combination of finite prime-power divisibility predicates; for b=0 it is universal. Modal diamonds reduce on each truth profile to the nonemptiness of an applicable test-free language and the uniform truth of their target formula, so arbitrary nested tests and negations are covered; boxes by duality. Conversely loop(a^m) together with exclusions loop(a^j) for 1≤j<m defines precisely n=m, and ¬loop((a^{p^e})*;a^{p^{e-1}}) defines p^e|n by modular closure. CRT gives the eventual gcd(n,M) characterization; totient residue counts give rational positive density for every infinite spectrum. A coprime residue argument shows n≡1(mod3) not definable. Independent direct finite modular-closure, prime-power and singleton witnesses corroborated the key arithmetic identities, not the infinite syntax induction. Scope excludes state labels, free propositions, program intersection, multiple unrelated programs and general-frame satisfiability; no tight complexity claim.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality: classical regular-language semilinearity, PDL looping semantics, general finite-satisfiability and variable-free translations are prior ingredients. The inspected primary theorems do not establish both the full exact-return fixed-cycle gcd spectrum and the converse prime-power/singleton definability under arbitrary nested formula tests. The stronger intersection language provides exact-return syntax but not an arithmetic spectrum classification. Actual full-text relevant material and published Resultary comparisons support a qualified PASS; older specialized permutation-cycle frame results remain a nonzero priority risk.
residual_risks: A historical result on variable-free loop dynamic logic over finite permutation cycles, perhaps indexed under finite cyclic algebras/monadic model theory, might already imply the complete gcd-spectrum theorem; priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The result completely characterizes the observable arithmetic of a natural, strong, parameter-free dynamic language on deterministic finite cycles. It demonstrates that even arbitrary regular-program star, converse, nested tests and exact-return loop cannot encode arbitrary ultimately periodic conditions such as a single nontrivial residue class, but exactly can encode singletons and every divisor predicate; it also identifies a positive-rational-density obstruction for infinite truth sets. Constructive expressiveness and impossibility in a natural infinite family of models are independently useful, beyond a renamed Parikh lemma or isolated computational examples.
